name: The Ledger
text: You count what every turn cost each side, and spend your damage only where the books say it pays.
source: cp101 — awarded with a midterm grade of B or better in Tempo & Resource, or after Santángel returns a ledger with no red ink.

name: On Curve
text: Your first turns use every point of Gold and every action; nothing is left on the table.
source: cp101 — attend at least five of the first six weeks of Tempo & Resource (weeks 4–5 teach it).

name: Priority Window
text: You know exactly when a Reaction may be played — and you make them use theirs at the worst moment.
source: rj101 — a final grade of B or better in Rules & Judging, or passing the Judge Circle's Level-1 mock exam (Day 57).

name: Count Your Outs
text: Before every draw you know how many cards save you and what the odds are.
source: ma101 — solve one of Dr. Blum's problems of the week on the board, or a midterm grade of B or better.

name: Table Hands
text: Shuffle, cut, present, announce: your hands know the routine even when your head has gone white.
source: cp150 — pass the Table Practicum midterm practical (Day 47), or play ten physical duels in front of witnesses.

name: Box Breath
text: Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Your pulse drops; the table stops swimming.
source: pc101 — complete the heartbeat drill under Coach Rox (week 3 onward), or be taught the same exercise by Nurse Camille in the infirmary.

name: Designer's Eye
text: You ask of every card what it wants to do — and see the opponent's plan in the pieces they chose.
source: gd110 — hand in the midterm design in Card Design Basics, or have Chuck take one of your card ideas seriously in his workshop.

name: The Long Record
text: You have studied how the great late-game decks of history were assembled, piece by quiet piece.
source: lh101 — a final essay graded B or better in Lore & History, or attending two of Chuck's visiting lectures and asking a real question.

name: Tape Study
text: You have watched them play before. Their habits are on film, and now in your head.
source: cm120 — sit in on three sessions of Analysis & VOD Review as an extra, or spend an evening in the replay booth with Bex or Pippa.

name: All-Out
text: When the last turns come you stop protecting anything and put every point into the kill.
source: lilia — she shows it once, after Rowan plays her without flinching (win or lose) or after she watches him win a match from behind.

name: Egg Timer
text: You let the early turns pass and set the pieces down in exactly the right order — patience with a stopwatch.
source: georgie — she explains it, very precisely and without looking up, once Rowan is a friend she trusts (playing her seriously, never talking down to her).

name: Bug Report
text: You find the one card their whole machine runs on and take it apart first.
source: rana — earned by testing with her for an evening without flinching at her temper; she hands over her matchup notes as if they were an insult.

name: Undertow
text: You stop fighting the board and let it come to you — then clear it in one pull when they are over-committed.
source: saoirse — a lesson at the boathouse, barefoot, after Rowan gets back on the surfboard a third time.

name: Stand Your Ground
text: When everything is coming at you, you answer only the thing that kills you and keep swinging with the rest.
source: baylee — he teaches it in about nine words after a shared day of real work (the orchard harvest, the gym, fixing the bungalow steps).

name: Hop Wide
text: You flood the board faster than one answer can deal with, and attack before they find the second.
source: inya — the prize for beating her, or the consolation for losing to her gracefully, in a best-of-three on the Commons ping-pong table.

name: Burn the Boats
text: Cornered, you stop defending altogether and make it a race they did not expect to be in.
source: willas — shouted across a practice table, then explained properly while he carries something heavy for Rowan. Available only while Willas is himself.

name: Clock Discipline
text: From the first turn you answer threats in the right order and never spend removal on the wrong one.
source: noor — taught at the Judge Circle or in a library carrel once she considers Rowan serious about the rules (attend the Circle twice, or ask her to explain the charter).

name: Zugzwang
text: In the last turns you leave them only moves that make their position worse.
source: dom — the Battle Team's vice-captain offers one analysis session to anyone who takes a game off a team member or reaches the ladder top 30.
